sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-4 / CR / 06(N)/ 2009-10 dated 10.03.2020 pertaining to Sy. No.50 measuring 0.02 guntas equivalent to 2178 Sq. feet of Chikkabidrakallu village, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka.

. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No. 1 bearing Sy. No.50 measuring 0.02 guntas equivalent to 2178 Sq. feet of Chikkabidrakallu village has been acquired under Preliminary Notification issued by the respondent No. 2 under Section 3A(1)
vide S.O. No.2000 (E) dated 22.11.2006 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1) and (2) vide S.O. No. 1923(E) dated 13.11.2007.
The respondent No.2 has passed the award on 10.04.2008 and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.1,25,000/- towards 2178 Sq. feet, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.

Subsequently, on 27.01.2009 the respondent No.1 has filed the application stating that the compensation fixed by the SLAO is less than the market value and hence, to enhance the compensation as per the NH Act, 1956.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.
Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:

:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
Further the respondent No. 2 ought to have followed Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act.
The respondent No. 2 has not made any attempt to investigate the market value of the subject lands as on the date of Preliminary Notification.

The respondent No. 2 held that as per the aforesaid notification, the guidance value of agricultural lands situated National Highways Authority Of India vs Shameem Banu on 6 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119223929/
2 at A.P. No.111/2021 Chikkabidrakalu was Rs.1,50,00,000/- per acre, NA lands was Rs.425/- per Sq. feet and that of gramathana was Rs.350/- per Sq. feet and in order to re- determine the market value for has taken the rate of Rs.1,50,00,000/-
per acre as the basis and the respondent No. 2 subtracted the amount awarded by the respondent No. 3 and already disbursed i.e., Rs. 25 lakhs per acre and arrived at 1,25,00,000/- per acre equivalent to Rs. 287/- per Sq. feet.

sentences.text:
The respondent No. 2 has held that the lands were abutting NH and that the lands acquired were commercial in nature on account of which the respondent No.1 is entitled to an addition of 75% on Rs. 287/- per Sq.
feet i.e., 287/- + Rs. 215/- (75% of Rs. 287/- and arrived at Rs. 502/- per Sq. feet.

In other words,
the respondent No. 2 enhanced the market value from Rs. 25 lakhs per acre equivalent to Rs. 57/-
per Sq. feet to Rs. 559/- per Sq. feet equivalent to Rs. 2,43,50,040/- per A.P. No.111/2021 acre.

The respondent No. 2 has added both 50% and 25% for National and State Highways to arrive at 75%
which is contrary to the special instruction given in the notification which provides for 50% and 25%
for National and State Highway receptively.
The respondent No.2 without assigning any reasons, in the operative portion of the impugned Arbitral Award has treated the agricultural lands as commercial lands which is completely arbitrary.
Among other grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

.5. The respondent No. 1 to 3 though served with the notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through DGP, the respondents 1 and 3 not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, they were placed exparte.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-4/CR/6(N)/2009-10 secured from the Arbitrator.

sentences.text: Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note the admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Mrs. Shameem Banu is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.50 measuring to an extent of 0.02 guntas equivalent to 2178 Sq. feet of Chikkabidrakallu village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-4 under Preliminary Notification dated 22.11.2006 and Final Notification dated 13.11.2007,
is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.3/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs.25 lakhs per acre equivalent to Rs.617.76 per Sq. meter.

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.1,25,000/- was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation.

.9. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 Mrs. A.P. No.111/2021 Shameem Banu filed an application before the respondent No.2 claiming that as the land is potential one and the commercial activities are carrying on in the acquired property, the annual income from the land is Rs. 15 lakhs per acre and further claiming that the non- agricultural land per Sq. feet is Rs.4,000/- ad Bore- well/well/pump set/pump house, servant quarters and fixtures etc., compound wall with gate, worth Rs. 2.5 lakhs and building fittings/fixtures/compound/worth Rs. 25 lakhs, number of trees worth Rs. 3 lakhs and hence, she is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs. 4,000/- per Sq. feet as on 27.01.2009.

The respondent No. 2 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.502 by adding of 75% A.P. No.111/2021 on Rs. 287/- per Sq. feet i.e., Rs. 287 + Rs.
215 (75% of Rs. 287/-) and arrived at Rs.502/- per Sq. feet, .10.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.2 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2007 published vide notification bearing No. CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007.
The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification was published as on 22.11.2006.
As such, the respondent No. 2 ought to have considered the market value of the property of the year 2006 and not of the year 2007.
As the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 17.04.2007 i.e., after lapse of more than 4 months from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
A.P. No.111/2021 It is true that as per the NH Act, the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

sentences.text: The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.

In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs.
National Highways Authority of India.

National Highways Authority of India

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.
However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.

In the case on hand, Subsequent to the notification bearing No.
CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007, the circular order not produced.
The LAO enhanced the compensation to the extent of 75% relying on the instructions applicable to the offices regarding valuation of the acquired property.

It is just and necessary to note the said guideline/instructions that reads as "The properties adjacent to National and State Highways for which rates have not been fixed in the rate list, additional rate at 50% and 25% of other properties shall be fixed respectively."

Therefore, if at all in the guideline value or market rates of the properties have not been fixed, then the aforesaid instructions is applicable for determining the market value in respect of the acquired property.
Accordingly, enhancement can be ordered.

.13. Now it is for the consideration of this court to see that how the said instructions or enhancement can be applied for the acquired property and how the arbitrator has applied the aforesaid instructions for A.P. No.111/2021 enhancement of compensation in the case on hand.

On perusal of the aforesaid guide line it is clear that the aforesaid guideline specifically applicable to the properties adjacent to the National and State Highways to which the guideline value has not been fixed or determined.
If the acquired land is adjacent to the National Highway and if no guidance value has been fixed, then the LAO can order for additional enhancement at the rate of 50%.

At the same time,
if the property adjacent to the State Highway, then additional rate of 25% can be added but both 50% and 25% together cannot be added.
In the case on hand, it appears that the LAO / respondent No.3 has added both 50% as well as 25% which is not permissible under law as per the aforesaid instructions.
In the case on hand, even if the claim of respondent No.1 is accepted, then the land is acquired for formation of widening of National Highways.

As such, the LAO ought to have enhanced only 50% which is prescribed for the land adjacent to the national highway and the 25% is A.P.
No.111/2021 prescribed for the land adjacent to the state highway which is not applicable to the land involved in this case.
As such, certainly this enhancement of respondent No.2/arbitrator cannot be accepted.

.14. In the case on hand, though the respondent No. 3 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the court to resist the case of the petitioner or to support the award passed by the respondent No.3.
Absolutely there is no material placed before the court to disbelieve the petitioner case or to substantiate the award passed by the respondent No.3.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.

Accordingly, the point No. 1 is held in the National Highways Authority Of India vs Shameem Banu on 6 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119223929/
